R9415.summary: Georgius, the dukes' servant, came back with three reasons for their urging concord at the diet of Pressburg. The 'enemy' king (Ferdinand) opened a treaty with King John while secretly suing the Sultan for peace; the Sultan's own letters revealed it, so John recalled his orators.
R9415.en:
Most illustrious princes, lords, as it were most renowned brothers, greeting and continual increase of perpetual
happiness. Your Lordships' servant Georgius ⟨.10.⟩ ⟨Marijo⟩ has come back to us, who in Your Lordships' name reported to
us the three chief reasons why he had so greatly urged that a concord be made with us at the diet of Pozsony. ⟨And indeed
all these things, which we have now also⟩ experienced in the event itself, under a certain feigned appearance?, whose
words Your Lordships' letters, brought to us afterwards by the Jew? ⟨.33.⟩? Marcus?, sufficiently confirmed. For the
[due]? goodwill of Your Lordships' mind towards us we give and hold great thanks to Your Lordships as to our most dear
lords and brothers, and, if ever an occasion of deserving it should offer itself, we promise our service and indeed all
our zeal in return.

R9411.summary: King John will do what he can for the dukes, but their request must first go to the governor (Lodovico Gritti) rather than straight to the Turkish emperor. He has begun on the gold and silver mines, sends his servant Nicolaus Freiberger, asks for skilled mining masters and for the Bavarian mining ordinance.
R9411.en:
Greeting and every good thing. Most illustrious princes, lords and dearest brothers. We have received Your
Lordships' letters, and the things which [..] we have also understood, which [..] they wrote [to?] their secretary.
May Your Lordships be persuaded that whatever we can do for the advantage and dignity of Your Lordships and of
their brothers and friends, we shall always do it with the greatest goodwill. And [..] in the business [..] for which
they now write, we shall gladly work; [..] it seems, however, that the matter must be communicated to the
illustrious lord governor of our kingdom, who [cumis] will shortly be here with us. For it seems better to us to
take his counsel on this matter than to try it abruptly with the most mighty emperor of the Turks [..].

R9412.summary: A German newsletter repeating news first sent on 22 December: what the chancellor Stephan Werbőczy obtained at the Porte (an everlasting peace between Hungary and the Turk, towns to be handed over such as Peterwardein, Titil and Salankamen, the kings' titles, the Sultan's letter); then plans against Siebenbürgen and the mines.
R9412.en:
Most gracious prince and lord, on 22 December I wrote to Your Grace similar news, but had to risk the letter with an
unreliable messenger; therefore I repeat the same news herewith: as, first, what the chancellor, Lord Stephan
Werbőczy, has achieved with the Turk. AND FIRST: he has made and concluded for Hungary an everlasting peace with the
Turk. SECONDLY: that all towns and places which [?His] [?Royal] [?Majesty] has held [within], contrary to it, are to
be handed over, namely Peterwardein and [Sarrus], with Titel, Salmaulack [Salankamen], the Secu, and the whole of
[?Syrmia]; hence, however, the wine that has grown there this year will be worth nothing. THIRDLY: [..] of the other

system: Homophonic substitution on a graphic sign set, no word division, a few signs carrying digraphs (ch, ck, sch) and three word signs; clear Latin passages left standing in the cipher. System L of the volume.
